text:
#The female employee at the parking ticket booth at the exit provided terrible service.
Around 7 PM, a female employee stood at the booth, saying 40 baht. We handed her cash. She stood there pressing buttons on her phone, pointing it at the booth while chewing gum, making faces, and then said, "Scan to pay only, no cash accepted. The system is closed at this time." Then she pulled a sour face.
My brother and I didn't know that cash couldn't be paid; we had to scan. We didn't have any money in our app, so my brother scanned instead. He was sitting in the back, and his phone was a bit slow, causing a delay of about two minutes. After he finished scanning, he showed us that it was done. The female employee said, "Didn't you want to see it, sir?" while bending down to look at the screen, asking if we wanted the receipt or not.
Seriously? People are sitting in their cars; should they get out to use their phones? What was the point of standing there if you're not going to take the receipt? We paid for parking here. You should improve your manners, girl.

text: The atmosphere is peaceful and serene, and temple festivals are held frequently.

The service is terrible. There's always been insufficient parking for motorcycles. Previously, there were three parking spots, but the center reduced that to two. If the parking lot is full, they tell you to park at the Makro store instead, which feels like they're shifting the burden onto others.

The chubby female employee supervising the parking lot seemed unwilling to work. She was making faces and being rude to customers. In customer service, she shouldn't treat customers like that. They're hired to work; they should help customers with their problems, not make faces as if they're asking for free parking.
Conveniently located near many shopping areas.

text: The female employee at the parking ticket booth at the exit provided terrible service. It's not even service-oriented. I simply asked about the ticket machine *politely*, but she responded rudely, rudely, and made a disgusted face as if she didn't realize she was providing customer service. I've seen many similar reviews; it's probably the same person. How is she still not fired? At the very least, she should have received a warning or retraining. Have some consideration for others who have to experience this.

text: Everything was great except for the toilet. Every time I came, the housekeeper never refilled the toilet paper, so I had to ask in the men's restroom. Today I asked again, and the housekeeper was reluctant. In short, she didn't refill it.

This place is truly a student hub, as you see lots of students walking around and reading. It's a small shopping and food area, not huge, just enough to satisfy your cravings. The restrooms aren't very clean, but the rest of the place is acceptable.

There's limited motorcycle parking, and the staff are neglectful. When customers move their motorcycles to make room, they're suddenly told not to park there, as if deliberately waiting for the customer to finish moving before being told. There's no sign of improvement.
Convenient to travel

text:
The head guard was unfriendly and spoke rudely.
Someone was eating and came up to me and said, "If you're full, get up so everyone else can eat." Is this really okay?
Suki Tee Noi restaurant is excellent. You hardly have to wait in line.

The female employee at the ticket booth at the exit had very bad manners. The booth said it was a card return slot. After returning the card, she looked displeased and asked for the card. I told her I had already returned it.

She had a very unpleasant tone and expression, telling me to wait for the barrier to lower before inserting the card. Who knew? Next time, please put up a sign to inform customers that they should wait for the car in front to go before inserting the card.

The sign on the booth even says it's a card return slot. Additional signage should be posted, and the employees should be thoroughly trained.
